name: UV tanning bed
lead: A UV tanning bed is a device with lamps that emit mostly UVA, with some UVB, to darken the skin. Commercial salons and home units exist.

It does produce a tan quickly, but the International Agency for Research on Cancer classifies UV-emitting tanning devices as carcinogenic to humans, and the wiki treats it as a hard skip in favor of DHA tanners.

paras: UV radiation damages skin cell DNA, which triggers melanin production and darkening; the tan is a response to injury. The same DNA damage drives photoaging and skin cancer.

Meta-analyses link indoor tanning to melanoma, with pooled relative risks of roughly 1.2 to 1.3, higher with early-age and frequent use, and to non-melanoma skin cancer. One 2013 analysis disputed the strength of the association in higher-quality studies. Tanning accelerates wrinkles, sunburn is common, and the claim of safe or healthy tanning is unsupported.
